q: Which zonal railway became the first zonal railway of Indian Railways to achieve complete electrification of its broad gauge network?
e: West Central Railway became the first zonal railway to achieve complete electrification of its broad gauge network, completing the work in 2021.

q: Which Mumbai suburban railway station became the first station in India to be managed entirely by women staff in 2017?
e: Matunga station on the Mumbai suburban railway became the first station in India managed entirely by women staff, in 2017.

q: India's first hydrogen-powered train is planned to be run in Haryana on the section between:
e: India's first hydrogen-powered train is planned to run in Haryana on the Jind-Sonipat section.

q: Which Indian train became the first train in India to be provided with an air-conditioned coach, in 1934?
e: The Frontier Mail became the first train in India to be provided with an air-conditioned coach, in 1934.

q: The first Humsafar Express of Indian Railways, introduced in 2016, was run between:
e: The first Humsafar Express, introduced in 2016 as a fully air-conditioned premium service, was run between Gorakhpur and Anand Vihar Terminal.

q: The Tamil epic 'Manimekalai', the sequel to the 'Silappadikaram' centred on the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi, was composed by:
e: Manimekalai, the Tamil epic sequel to Silappadikaram centred on the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi, was composed by Sattanar.

q: The 'Ashtadhyayi', the celebrated Sanskrit treatise on grammar composed in eight chapters, was written by:
e: The Ashtadhyayi, the celebrated Sanskrit grammar in eight chapters, was written by Panini.

q: The 'Amarakosha', a famous Sanskrit thesaurus of synonyms also known as the 'Namalinganushasanam', was compiled by:
e: The Amarakosha, the famous Sanskrit thesaurus also known as Namalinganushasanam, was compiled by Amarasimha.

q: The 'Kamasutra', the ancient Sanskrit text on love, pleasure and social conduct, is attributed to:
e: The Kamasutra, the ancient Sanskrit text on love, pleasure and social conduct, is attributed to Vatsyayana.

q: The 'Yoga Sutras', the foundational text of classical Yoga philosophy, were compiled by:
e: The Yoga Sutras, the foundational text of classical Yoga philosophy, were compiled by Patanjali.

q: The Sanskrit prose romance 'Dashakumaracharita' (The Tale of the Ten Princes) was written by:
e: Dashakumaracharita, the Sanskrit prose romance of the ten princes, was written by Dandin.

q: The 'Brihatkatha', the great Sanskrit ocean of tales composed in the Paisachi language and now lost in its original form, is attributed to:
e: The Brihatkatha, the great ocean of tales composed in the Paisachi language and now lost in its original form, is attributed to Gunadhya.

q: The 'Ashtangahridaya', one of the principal treatises of Ayurveda synthesising the teachings of Charaka and Sushruta, was compiled by:
e: The Ashtangahridaya, a principal Ayurveda treatise synthesising Charaka and Sushruta, was compiled by Vagbhata.

q: The Sanskrit mahakavya 'Kiratarjuniya', based on the encounter between Arjuna and Lord Shiva in the guise of a Kirata (hunter), was composed by:
e: Kiratarjuniya, the Sanskrit mahakavya on Arjuna's encounter with Shiva disguised as a Kirata hunter, was composed by Bharavi.

q: The Sanskrit mahakavya 'Shishupalavadha', centred on the slaying of Shishupala by Lord Krishna, was composed by:
e: Shishupalavadha, the Sanskrit mahakavya centred on Krishna's slaying of Shishupala, was composed by Magha.

q: The Odia novel 'Chha Mana Atha Guntha' (Six Acres and a Third), regarded as the first major novel in Odia literature, was written by:
e: Chha Mana Atha Guntha (Six Acres and a Third), regarded as the first major Odia novel, was written by Fakir Mohan Senapati.

q: The celebrated Telugu play 'Kanyasulkam', a satire on the social evil of bride-price, was written by:
e: Kanyasulkam, the celebrated Telugu play satirising the evil of bride-price, was written by Gurajada Apparao.

q: The Kannada novel 'Samskara' (1965), centred on the moral dilemma of the orthodox scholar Praneshacharya, was written by:
e: Samskara (1965), the Kannada novel on the moral dilemma of the orthodox scholar Praneshacharya, was written by U. R. Ananthamurthy.

q: The Victorian novel 'Middlemarch' (1871-72), subtitled 'A Study of Provincial Life', was written by:
e: Middlemarch (1871-72), subtitled A Study of Provincial Life, was written by George Eliot, the pen name of Mary Ann Evans.

q: The celebrated collection of poetry 'Leaves of Grass', first published in 1855 and enlarged by its author throughout his life, was written by:
e: Leaves of Grass, first published in 1855 and enlarged by its author throughout his life, was written by the American poet Walt Whitman.

q: The Russian novel 'Fathers and Sons' (1862), famous for its young nihilist hero Bazarov, was written by:
e: Fathers and Sons (1862), famous for its young nihilist hero Bazarov, was written by the Russian novelist Ivan Turgenev.

q: The Raleigh Commission (1902), whose report led to the enactment of the Indian Universities Act of 1904, was appointed to inquire into:

options.B: The condition and prospects of the universities in India
options.C: The superior civil services in India

e: The Raleigh Commission (1902) inquired into the condition and prospects of the universities in India, and its report led to the Indian Universities Act of 1904.

q: The Royal Commission on Agriculture in India (1926), which reported on the condition of agriculture and the rural economy, was chaired by:
e: The Royal Commission on Agriculture in India (1926), which reported on agriculture and the rural economy, was chaired by Lord Linlithgow.

q: The first Famine Commission (1880), whose report led to the formulation of the Famine Code, was chaired by:
e: The first Famine Commission (1880), whose report led to the formulation of the Famine Code, was chaired by Sir Richard Strachey.

q: The Zakir Husain Committee (1937), appointed after the Wardha Conference, drew up the detailed scheme of:
e: The Zakir Husain Committee (1937), appointed after the Wardha Conference, drew up the detailed scheme of Basic Education, or Nai Talim.

q: The Calendar Reform Committee (1952), whose recommendations led to the adoption of the Indian national calendar, was chaired by:
e: The Calendar Reform Committee (1952), whose recommendations led to adoption of the Indian national calendar, was chaired by the scientist Meghnad Saha.

q: The Gore Committee (1971), appointed by the Ministry of Home Affairs, is associated with recommendations on:
e: The Gore Committee (1971), appointed by the Ministry of Home Affairs, made recommendations on police training in India.

q: The First National Commission on Labour (1966), which reviewed the conditions of labour and the working of labour legislation since Independence, was chaired by:
e: The First National Commission on Labour (1966), which reviewed labour conditions and labour legislation since Independence, was chaired by Justice P. B. Gajendragadkar.

q: The Scott-Moncrieff Commission (1901), also known as the Indian Irrigation Commission, was appointed to report on:

options.C: The development of irrigation in India

e: The Scott-Moncrieff Commission (1901), the Indian Irrigation Commission, was appointed to report on the development of irrigation in India.

q: The Kartar Singh Committee (1973), appointed by the Ministry of Health and Family Planning, is best known for recommending:

options.D: A separate cadre for rural postings of nurses

e: The Kartar Singh Committee (1973) is best known for recommending the multipurpose health worker scheme for rural health services.

q: The Shekatkar Committee (2016), headed by Lt. Gen. (Retd.) D. B. Shekatkar, was set up by the Ministry of Defence to recommend measures for:

options.C: Reform of the civil services examination
options.D: Enhancing combat capability and rebalancing defence expenditure

e: The Shekatkar Committee (2016) was set up by the Ministry of Defence to recommend measures for enhancing combat capability and rebalancing defence expenditure.

q: The Third Finance Commission of India, constituted in 1960, was chaired by:
e: The Third Finance Commission of India, constituted in 1960, was chaired by A. K. Chanda.

q: The Sixth Finance Commission of India, constituted in 1972, was chaired by:
e: The Sixth Finance Commission of India, constituted in 1972, was chaired by K. Brahmananda Reddy.

q: The 'Forint' is the currency of:
e: The Forint is the currency of Hungary; Poland uses the Zloty and Bulgaria the Lev.

q: Baku is the capital of:
e: Baku, situated on the western shore of the Caspian Sea, is the capital and largest city of Azerbaijan.

q: The Parliament of Germany is known as the:
e: The Bundestag is the Parliament of Germany, its federal lower house; the Bundesrat represents the states.

q: Mount Kosciuszko, rising in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales, is the highest peak of:
e: Mount Kosciuszko, in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales, is the highest peak of mainland Australia.

q: The scientific study of fishes is known as:
e: Ichthyology is the scientific study of fishes; entomology studies insects and ornithology studies birds.

q: The 'Tugrik' is the currency of:
e: The Tugrik is the currency of Mongolia, the landlocked East Asian country whose capital is Ulaanbaatar.

q: Tbilisi is the capital of:
e: Tbilisi, situated on the banks of the Kura River, is the capital and largest city of Georgia in the Caucasus.

q: The lower house of the Parliament of Russia (the Federal Assembly) is known as the:
e: The State Duma is the lower house of the Federal Assembly, the Parliament of Russia.

q: Denali, the highest mountain peak of North America, is located in the United States State of:
e: Denali, the highest peak of North America, is located in the US State of Alaska.

q: The scientific study of earthquakes and the propagation of seismic waves through the Earth is known as:
e: Seismology is the scientific study of earthquakes and the propagation of seismic waves through the Earth.

q: The longest river of Australia is the:
e: The Murray River is the longest river of Australia, forming much of the New South Wales-Victoria border.

q: Yerevan is the capital of:
e: Yerevan is the capital and largest city of Armenia, the landlocked country in the Caucasus region.

q: 'Washing soda', widely used as a water softener and cleaning agent, is chemically:
e: Washing soda, used as a water softener and cleaning agent, is chemically sodium carbonate.

q: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is located at Nairobi in Kenya.

q: The Beas River originates at Beas Kund, a small glacial lake situated near the:
e: The Beas River originates at Beas Kund, a small glacial lake near the Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh.

q: 'Green vitriol', a green crystalline salt used in ink making and as a mordant, is chemically:
e: Green vitriol, the green crystalline salt used in ink making and as a mordant, is chemically ferrous sulphate.

q: The headquarters of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is located at Lausanne in Switzerland.

q: The Railway Service Commissions, set up for the recruitment of subordinate staff on Indian Railways, were renamed as Railway Recruitment Boards in the year:
e: The Railway Service Commissions, set up to recruit subordinate railway staff, were renamed Railway Recruitment Boards in 1985, and the RRBs continue to conduct recruitment for non-gazetted posts.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IRIMEE) at Jamalpur mainly imparts training to the officers of which department of Indian Railways?
e: IRIMEE at Jamalpur is the specialised training institute for Mechanical Engineering officers, covering locomotive, carriage and wagon and workshop technology.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Electrical Engineering (IRIEEN) at Nasik Road mainly imparts training to the officers of which department of Indian Railways?
e: IRIEEN at Nasik Road is the specialised institute for Electrical Engineering officers, training them in traction, power supply and electrical services.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Transport Management (IRITM) at Lucknow mainly imparts training in which field of railway working?

options.D: Transport Management for Traffic Department officers

e: IRITM at Lucknow imparts training in Transport Management to Traffic Department officers, covering operations, commercial working and transport economics.

q: Each Bench of the Railway Claims Tribunal consists of:

options.B: One Judicial Member and one Technical Member
options.D: One Judicial Member and one Accounts Member

e: Each Bench of the Railway Claims Tribunal consists of one Judicial Member and one Technical Member, combining legal and railway expertise for deciding claims cases.

q: The Operation Control Centre (OCC) of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, from where the corridor's train operations are monitored, is located at:
e: The Operation Control Centre of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor is located at Ahmedabad, from where train operations over the corridor are monitored and controlled.

q: The Buddhist Circuit Special Train, run for tourists visiting the Buddhist pilgrimage centres, is operated by:

options.A: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)

e: The Buddhist Circuit Special Train, visiting centres linked with the life of Buddha, is operated by IRCTC, the tourism and catering arm of Indian Railways.

q: After the restructuring of the Railway Board in 2020, the Board, apart from the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, consists of how many Members?
e: After the 2020 restructuring, the Railway Board consists of the Chairman and CEO plus four Members, each looking after a major functional area.

q: The All India Railwaymen's Federation (AIRF), one of the two recognised federations of railway employees, was founded in the year:
e: The All India Railwaymen's Federation, a recognised federation of railway employees, was founded in 1924 and is among the oldest railway trade unions in India.

q: The Chhattisgarh Railway Corporation Limited has been set up mainly to execute which rail corridor project in Chhattisgarh?
e: Chhattisgarh Railway Corporation Limited was set up mainly to execute the Katghora-Dongargarh new railway line project in Chhattisgarh through a joint venture model.

q: Braithwaite, Burn and Jessop Construction Company Limited (BBJ), the railway public sector undertaking, is well known for having constructed which landmark bridge?
e: BBJ is famed for constructing the Howrah Bridge, now Rabindra Setu, the steel cantilever bridge over the Hooghly at Kolkata completed in 1943.

q: The Golden Chariot luxury tourist train of Karnataka is presently operated and marketed by:

options.D: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)

e: The Golden Chariot, Karnataka's luxury tourist train, is presently operated and marketed by IRCTC, which took over its operation from the state tourism corporation.

q: The Zonal Railway Training Institute (ZRTI) at Moula Ali in Hyderabad functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Moula Ali, Hyderabad, functions under South Central Railway, whose headquarters is at Secunderabad.

q: The North-South (Blue Line) corridor of the Kolkata Metro, the oldest metro corridor of the city, is operated by:
e: The North-South Blue Line of Kolkata Metro, the city's oldest metro corridor, is operated by Metro Railway, Kolkata, a zonal railway of Indian Railways.

q: Lucknow is the headquarters of two railway divisions bearing the same name, Lucknow division, which function under the:

options.A: Northern Railway and North Eastern Railway
options.B: Northern Railway and North Central Railway
options.C: North Eastern Railway and East Central Railway
options.D: Northern Railway and West Central Railway

e: Lucknow has two divisions of the same name, one under Northern Railway and the other under North Eastern Railway, serving different routes from the city.

q: The Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya division of Indian Railways, earlier known as the Mughalsarai division, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya division, earlier called Mughalsarai division, belongs to East Central Railway, headquartered at Hajipur.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Sabarmati in Ahmedabad functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Sabarmati, Ahmedabad, functions under Western Railway, which administers rail operations in Gujarat and adjoining areas.

q: The Coach Rehabilitation Workshop (CRWS) at Nishatpura in Bhopal, which undertakes rehabilitation and overhaul of passenger coaches, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Coach Rehabilitation Workshop at Nishatpura, Bhopal, functions under West Central Railway, headquartered at Jabalpur.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Samastipur in Bihar functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Samastipur in Bihar functions under East Central Railway, the zone covering Samastipur division.

q: The Rail Coach Naveenikaran Karkhana at Barhi near Sonipat, a production unit of Indian Railways, is mainly engaged in:

options.D: Refurbishment and mid-life rehabilitation of passenger coaches

e: Rail Coach Naveenikaran Karkhana at Barhi near Sonipat is engaged in refurbishment and mid-life rehabilitation of passenger coaches, giving them a renewed service life.

q: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at New Bongaigaon in Assam functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at New Bongaigaon in Assam functions under Northeast Frontier Railway, headquartered at Maligaon, Guwahati.

q: The Chittaranjan Locomotive Works (CLW) at Chittaranjan is located in which district of West Bengal?
e: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works at Chittaranjan is located in Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal, near Asansol.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Jabalpur functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Jabalpur functions under West Central Railway, whose headquarters is itself at Jabalpur.

q: The Northern Railway, one of the present zonal railways of Indian Railways, was formed in the year:
e: Northern Railway, headquartered in New Delhi, was formed in 1952 by merging the Jodhpur, Bikaner and Delhi divisions with the East Punjab Railway.

q: In the Accounts Department of Indian Railways, the designation 'FA&CAO' stands for:

options.A: Finance Assistant and Chief Audit Officer
options.C: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.D: Finance Adviser and Commercial Accounts Officer

e: FA and CAO stands for Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer, the head of the Accounts Department at zonal railway headquarters.

q: In the divisional accounts organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'Sr. DFM' stands for:
e: Sr. DFM stands for Senior Divisional Finance Manager, the senior Accounts officer at divisional level who heads the divisional finance and accounts office.

q: In the Accounts Department of Indian Railways, the post 'AFA', to which appointments are made through the Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, stands for:
e: AFA stands for Assistant Financial Adviser, the gazetted Accounts post in Indian Railways to which appointments are made through the LDCE.

q: In the stock verification organisation of the railway Accounts Department, the abbreviation 'ASV' stands for:
e: ASV stands for Assistant Stock Verifier, the Accounts Department official who carries out physical verification of stores and materials.

q: In the Railway Protection Force, the designation 'DSC', borne by the head of the force at the divisional level, stands for:
e: DSC stands for Divisional Security Commissioner, the Railway Protection Force officer heading the force at divisional level.

q: In the workshop accounts organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'WAO' stands for:
e: WAO stands for Workshop Accounts Officer, the Accounts officer in charge of the accounts office attached to a railway workshop.

q: In the freight infrastructure of Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'MMLP' stands for:
e: MMLP stands for Multi-Modal Logistics Park, a freight facility integrating road, rail and other modes with warehousing and logistics services.

q: In Government procurement, the portal denoted by the abbreviation 'CPPP' stands for:
e: CPPP stands for Central Public Procurement Portal, the Government of India's portal for e-procurement and publication of tenders by central organisations.

q: In railway engineering works for the elimination of level crossings, the structure denoted by 'RUB' stands for:
e: RUB stands for Road Under Bridge, a structure taking a road below the railway track to eliminate a level crossing.

q: In the elimination of manned level crossings on Indian Railways, the low-cost structure denoted by 'LHS' stands for:
e: LHS stands for Limited Height Subway, a low-cost structure of restricted height built in place of a manned level crossing for light vehicles and pedestrians.

q: In railway security, the abbreviation 'CORAS', the commando unit of the Railway Protection Force, stands for:

options.D: Commandos for Rail and Station Security

e: CORAS, the commando unit of the Railway Protection Force raised for rail and station security, is expanded in the key as Commando for Railway Security.

q: The first train run under the 'Bharat Gaurav' scheme by a private service provider, South Star Rail in June 2022, ran between:
e: The first Bharat Gaurav train by a private service provider, South Star Rail in June 2022, ran between Coimbatore North and Sainagar Shirdi.

q: The main arch span of the Chenab Rail Bridge of the USBRL project, the world's highest railway arch bridge, is about:
e: The Chenab Rail Bridge of the USBRL project, the world's highest railway arch bridge, has a main arch span of about 467 metres.

q: The total length of the Anji Khad Bridge, India's first cable-stayed railway bridge built as part of the USBRL project, is about:
e: The Anji Khad Bridge, India's first cable-stayed railway bridge on the USBRL project, has a total length of about 725 metres.

q: The 21 km long tunnel of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor includes an undersea section beneath the Thane Creek, whose length is about:
e: The 21 km tunnel of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor includes an undersea section of about 7 km beneath Thane Creek.

q: The first (priority) corridor of the Kanpur Metro, inaugurated in December 2021, connects:
e: The first priority corridor of Kanpur Metro, inaugurated in December 2021, connects IIT Kanpur with Motijheel.

q: The first section of the Lucknow Metro, opened for public service in September 2017, ran between:
e: The first section of Lucknow Metro, opened in September 2017, ran between Transport Nagar and Charbagh.

q: The first stretch of the Kochi Metro, opened in June 2017, ran between:
e: The first stretch of Kochi Metro, opened in June 2017, ran between Aluva and Palarivattom.

q: The Hyderabad Metro Rail, inaugurated in November 2017, initially opened for public service between:
e: Hyderabad Metro Rail, inaugurated in November 2017, initially opened for public service between Miyapur and Nagole.

q: In October 2024, the Ministry of Railways signed a Memorandum of Understanding for technical cooperation in the railway sector with which European country?
e: In October 2024 the Ministry of Railways signed an MoU for technical cooperation in the railway sector with Switzerland.

q: The first line of the Jaipur Metro, the Pink Line opened in June 2015, ran between:
e: The first line of Jaipur Metro, the Pink Line opened in June 2015, ran between Mansarovar and Chandpole.

q: The novel 'The Good Earth' (1931), depicting the life of a Chinese farmer and his family, was written by:
e: The Good Earth (1931), depicting Chinese farmer Wang Lung and his family, was written by Pearl S. Buck, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

q: The science-fiction novel 'Dune' (1965), set on the desert planet Arrakis, was written by:
e: Dune (1965), the science-fiction novel set on the desert planet Arrakis, was written by Frank Herbert.

q: The novel 'The Remains of the Day' (1989), narrated by the English butler Stevens, was written by:
e: The Remains of the Day (1989), narrated by the English butler Stevens, was written by Kazuo Ishiguro and won the Booker Prize.

q: The novel 'Atonement' (2001), centred on the young writer Briony Tallis and a fateful accusation, was written by:
e: Atonement (2001), centred on young writer Briony Tallis and her fateful accusation, was written by Ian McEwan.

q: The historical novel 'Wolf Hall' (2009), centred on Thomas Cromwell at the court of Henry VIII, was written by:
e: Wolf Hall (2009), centred on Thomas Cromwell at the court of Henry VIII, was written by Hilary Mantel and won the Booker Prize.
